days.title: The life of a request
days.tagline: What happens between pressing Enter and seeing a response, hop by hop.

lessons.title: Clients, servers, and the contract between them
lessons.scope: Client-server model, request-response cycle, what 'backend' covers, statelessness, the difference between the protocol, the server process, and the application code.

lessons.title: From URL to bytes: DNS, TCP, TLS
lessons.scope: URL anatomy, DNS resolution and caching (TTL), TCP handshake and ports, TLS handshake and certificates, where connection setup time goes, connection reuse.

lessons.title: Inside the datacenter: proxy, app, database
lessons.scope: CDN, load balancer, reverse proxy (nginx), app server, database, cache, and back. What each hop adds and what each hop can break. Time to first byte.

lessons.title: Which hop is lying? A map for debugging
lessons.scope: Using the hop map to localize a fault: DNS vs connect vs TLS vs server vs app vs DB. Browser devtools network timing, curl -v output read as evidence, the idea of bisecting the path.

mustCover: one long-lived connection vs many short ones
terminating TLS at the load balancer vs at the app
failureSignatures: DNS failure vs connection refused vs connection timeout vs TLS error vs 5xx: what each proves about how far the request got

days.title: HTTP, read fluently
days.tagline: Methods, status codes, and headers as a diagnostic language.

lessons.title: Anatomy of a request and a response
lessons.scope: Start line, headers, body; content types and encodings; query string vs path vs body; reading a raw exchange line by line.

lessons.title: Methods, safety, and idempotency
lessons.scope: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS, HEAD; safe vs idempotent; why idempotency decides what can be retried.

lessons.title: Status codes tell you where the fault is
lessons.scope: 2xx, 3xx, 4xx, 5xx families; 400 vs 401 vs 403 vs 404 vs 409 vs 422 vs 429; 500 vs 502 vs 503 vs 504 and who emitted each; redirects.

lessons.title: Headers, cookies, CORS, and HTTP versions
lessons.scope: Headers that change behavior (Content-Type, Authorization, Cache-Control, Accept, User-Agent, X-Request-ID); cookies and their flags; CORS and preflight as a browser rule; HTTP/1.1 vs HTTP/2 vs HTTP/3; keep-alive and timeouts.

failureSignatures: CORS error in the browser while curl works
wrong Content-Type producing 415 or 422
a retried POST creating duplicates

days.title: Inside the server: concurrency and runtimes
days.tagline: How one machine serves thousands of requests, and what each language trades to do it.

lessons.title: What a server process does all day
lessons.scope: Listening socket, accept loop, worker models (process per worker, thread pool, event loop), ASGI/WSGI in Python terms, what 'a worker is busy' means.

lessons.title: Threads, event loops, and coroutines
lessons.scope: Concurrency vs parallelism; blocking vs non-blocking I/O; async/await as cooperative scheduling; the Python GIL; what blocks an event loop and how it shows up.

lessons.title: CPU-bound vs I/O-bound, pools, and backpressure
lessons.scope: Classifying work; connection pools and pool exhaustion; queues inside the server; backpressure; memory growth and garbage collection pauses.

lessons.title: Languages and runtimes: Python, Node, Go, Java, PHP
lessons.scope: What each runtime optimizes: concurrency model, raw speed, ecosystem, deployment shape, typical failure modes. How to reason about a choice, and why most teams should not switch languages to fix a slow endpoint.

mustCover: language choice tradeoffs across Python, JavaScript, Go, Java, PHP
failureSignatures: one slow sync call inside async code stalls every request
connection pool exhausted
all workers busy while CPU is idle
memory climbs until the process is killed

days.title: API design: REST done properly
days.tagline: Resources, pagination, errors, idempotency, and changing an API without breaking its clients.

lessons.title: Resources, verbs, and statelessness
lessons.scope: Modeling nouns and relationships, URL design, using methods and status codes consistently, why statelessness helps scaling and debugging.

lessons.title: Pagination, filtering, and error shapes
lessons.scope: Offset vs cursor pagination, sorting and filtering conventions, consistent machine-readable errors, validation at the edge.

lessons.title: Idempotency keys, retries, and rate limits
lessons.scope: Why networks force retries, idempotency keys for POST, rate limiting algorithms at concept level (fixed window, sliding window, token bucket), 429 and Retry-After.

lessons.title: Contracts and versioning
lessons.scope: OpenAPI as a contract, backward-compatible vs breaking changes, versioning strategies, deprecation, why contract drift is a top source of integration bugs.

mustCover: URL versioning vs header versioning vs additive evolution
failureSignatures: duplicate or missing rows while paging
client broke after a field rename
double charge after a timeout and retry
sudden 429s from one noisy client

days.title: Beyond REST: GraphQL, gRPC, streaming, webhooks

lessons.title: GraphQL: the client chooses the shape
lessons.scope: Schema, queries, mutations, resolvers; over-fetching and under-fetching; the N+1 resolver problem; caching and authorization difficulties; errors inside a 200.

lessons.title: gRPC and protobuf: contracts between services
lessons.scope: Protobuf schemas and code generation, HTTP/2 transport, unary vs streaming calls, deadlines and status codes, schema evolution rules, why browsers need a proxy.

lessons.title: Real time: polling, SSE, WebSockets
lessons.scope: Short polling, long polling, server-sent events, WebSockets; how LLM token streaming uses SSE; proxies, timeouts, and reconnects.

lessons.title: Webhooks, and choosing a style
lessons.scope: Webhooks as reverse APIs: signatures, retries, ordering, replay; a decision guide for REST vs GraphQL vs gRPC vs events.

failureSignatures: GraphQL returns 200 with an errors array
stream cuts off at exactly 60 seconds
webhook delivered twice or out of order
gRPC DEADLINE_EXCEEDED

days.title: Debugging as a method
days.tagline: A repeatable loop for going from 'it is broken' to the line, config, or row that broke it.

lessons.title: The loop: observe, hypothesize, test, narrow
lessons.scope: Debugging as experiments; stating the expected vs the actual precisely; one change at a time; keeping a log of what was ruled out; the first question, 'what changed?'.

lessons.title: Reproduce and reduce

lessons.title: Bisecting everything
lessons.scope: Binary search over commits (git bisect), over layers of the request path, over config, over data, over time. Why halving beats guessing.

lessons.title: Reading errors and stack traces, and the traps
lessons.scope: Reading a Python traceback bottom up, root cause vs symptom, chained exceptions, swallowed errors; cognitive traps: confirmation bias, fixing the symptom, assuming the newest code is at fault, trusting a stale log.

failureSignatures: works locally and fails in production
fails one time in fifty

the fix made the error disappear without explaining it

days.title: Observability: logs, metrics, traces
days.tagline: The three signals, what question each answers, and how to connect them.

lessons.title: Logs worth reading
lessons.scope: Structured logs, levels, request and correlation IDs, what to log and what never to log (secrets, personal data), log volume and sampling.

lessons.title: Metrics and percentiles
lessons.scope: Counters, gauges, histograms; rate, errors, duration (RED) and utilization, saturation, errors (USE); p50 vs p95 vs p99 and why averages hide problems; cardinality.

lessons.title: Traces and spans
lessons.scope: A trace as a tree of timed spans, context propagation across services and queues, reading a waterfall, OpenTelemetry in one paragraph, sampling.

lessons.title: SLOs, alerts, and what to instrument first

a metric with exploding cardinality

days.title: Indexes and the query planner

lessons.title: Why a query is slow: scans
lessons.scope: Sequential scan vs index scan, how row count changes everything, selectivity, why the same query is fast in development and slow in production.

lessons.title: Indexes: B-tree, composite, covering
lessons.scope: A B-tree as a sorted lookup structure, column order in composite indexes, covering indexes, partial and unique indexes, the write and storage cost of each index.

lessons.title: Reading a query plan
lessons.scope: EXPLAIN and EXPLAIN ANALYZE output read line by line: estimated vs actual rows, node types, where time goes, stale statistics.

lessons.title: The usual suspects: N+1, pools, long queries
lessons.scope: N+1 queries from ORMs, missing index on a foreign key, SELECT *, unbounded result sets, connection pooling and PgBouncer, slow query logs, table bloat in one paragraph.

mustCover: composite index vs several single-column indexes
fixing the query vs adding hardware
failureSignatures: endpoint slows as the table grows

days.title: Transactions and concurrency

lessons.title: Isolation levels and their anomalies

lessons.title: Locks, MVCC, and deadlocks

lessons.scope: Fixed workflows vs model-directed loops, orchestrator and worker patterns, handoffs and context loss, the Model Context Protocol as a standard for tools.

lessons.title: Failure modes, safety, and reading a trajectory
lessons.scope: Loops, tool misuse, compounding errors, premature stopping, context overflow, prompt injection through tool results; sandboxing and permissions; human approval; reading a run trace step by step.

mustCover: more tools vs fewer sharper tools
failureSignatures: agent repeats the same failing tool call
agent declares success without verifying
run degrades after context compaction
tool result contains instructions the agent follows
cost grows with every turn

days.title: Evaluating LLM and agent systems
days.tagline: Evals are the tests of a non-deterministic system. Building them well is most of the job.

lessons.title: Evals vs tests
lessons.scope: Why exact-match assertions fail for model output, pass rates instead of pass or fail, capability evals vs regression evals, what an eval result does and does not prove.

lessons.title: Datasets and graders
lessons.scope: Building an eval set from real failures and realistic tasks, held-out data, code-based graders, LLM-as-judge and its calibration, human review, grader bugs.

lessons.title: Statistics for evals
lessons.scope: Variance across runs, sample size, confidence intervals, comparing two versions, multiple trials per task, why a two-point change on fifty samples means little.

lessons.title: Agent evals, online evals, and debugging an eval
lessons.scope: Outcome grading vs trajectory grading, checking environment state, resetting sandboxes, infrastructure failures counted as model failures; A/B tests and production signals; Goodhart's law, contamination, and overfitting to the eval.

mustCover: code grader vs LLM judge vs human
offline eval vs online A/B test
grading the outcome vs grading the trajectory
large noisy eval vs small careful eval
failureSignatures: score moved and nobody knows whether it is noise
eval passes while users complain
a grader that accepts wrong answers
failures caused by the harness timing out
eval set leaked into the prompt or training data

days.title: Reinforcement learning
days.tagline: Learning from reward: the loop, the algorithm families, and why the agent optimizes what you measured.

lessons.title: The RL loop: states, actions, rewards
lessons.scope: Agent and environment, episodes, return and discounting, the Markov decision process as a frame, exploration vs exploitation, bandits as the simplest case.

lessons.title: Value, policy, and the algorithm families
lessons.scope: Value functions and policies; value-based methods (Q-learning, DQN), policy gradients (REINFORCE, PPO), actor-critic; on-policy vs off-policy; model-free vs model-based. Concepts and tradeoffs only.

lessons.title: Reward design and reward hacking
lessons.scope: Sparse vs dense rewards, credit assignment, reward shaping, specification gaming with concrete examples, why a rising reward curve is not proof of the behavior you wanted.

lessons.title: RL for LLMs and agents, and why runs are hard to debug
lessons.scope: RL from human feedback, RL on agent tasks with graders and verifiers as reward, environments and their bugs, instability, seed sensitivity, reproducibility, offline RL in brief.

failureSignatures: reward climbs while the task is not being solved
results differ wildly across seeds
policy collapses to one action
agent exploits a bug in the environment or grader

days.title: Training and serving infrastructure
days.tagline: Data pipelines, GPUs, checkpoints, and the signals that tell you a run is healthy.

lessons.title: The training pipeline end to end
lessons.scope: Data collection, cleaning, versioning, tokenization, the training loop, checkpoints, evaluation; GPUs, memory, and batch size; distributed training and mixed precision at concept level.

lessons.title: Reading a training run
lessons.scope: Loss curves: healthy, diverging, plateaued, overfitting, NaN; learning rate and warmup, gradient clipping; experiment tracking; changing one thing at a time.

lessons.title: Serving models
lessons.scope: Latency vs throughput on GPUs, dynamic batching, quantization and distillation, token streaming, autoscaling and cold starts, hosted API vs self-hosted model.

lessons.title: MLOps: versioning, drift, and reproducibility
lessons.scope: Versioning data, code, config, and weights together; model registry and staged rollout; monitoring data drift and quality in production; feedback loops; how MLOps differs from DevOps.

failureSignatures: loss becomes NaN
out-of-memory on the GPU
cannot reproduce last week's result
quality decays slowly in production
training resumed from the wrong checkpoint

days.title: Capstone: incidents across the whole stack
days.tagline: Six incidents that cross layers, then the final exam.

lessons.title: The master map: from symptom to layer
lessons.scope: A synthesis lesson. One decision procedure that starts from the symptom (error, slow, wrong, intermittent, costly) and narrows to a layer: network, HTTP, app runtime, database, cache, queue, dependency, deploy, model, retrieval, agent harness, eval.

lessons.title: The tradeoff ledger
lessons.scope: A synthesis lesson. The recurring tradeoffs of the month side by side: consistency vs availability, latency vs throughput, simplicity vs flexibility, speed of change vs safety, cost vs quality, determinism vs capability.

lessons.title: Keeping the skill
lessons.scope: A short lesson on practice after day 30: write postmortems for your own bugs, keep a debugging journal, read one incident report a week, turn each failure into a regression test or eval case.

mustCover: cross-layer reasoning: each drill must involve at least two different days' topics, and at least three drills must involve the AI system (LLM calls, RAG, agent, or eval harness) interacting with classic backend parts
failureSignatures: a symptom whose obvious cause is wrong
two simultaneous changes
an eval regression caused by infrastructure
a cache or queue masking the real fault
